big: A REIT pays ₹10 a unit. A client calls it all income and plans tax on it. But the ₹10 is a mix: interest, dividend, rent, and maybe return of capital. Each part is treated differently.

lines: The website says 7% yield. Is that what I keep?
No. That yield is before tax and before splitting the payout into parts. Interest, dividend and rent are generally taxed at slab rates. Return of capital is not income, but it lowers your cost.

note: Check the REIT's component-wise statement. Rules change. Confirm with a tax adviser.
